designs.title: Probably Fine
designs.why: Clean, consistent monoline icon set with one stroke weight. It reads as a tidy graphic block from 3 m, and PROBABLY FINE. lands the deadpan joke. But the check-engine-light joke is a well-worn meme, and at $50 it needs more ownership. The 16 labels shrink to near-illegible on the tee. The headline sits jammed under the bottom label row with almost no breathing room. A couple of icons (traction control, airbag) are muddy or non-standard, which car people will notice.
designs.fix: Give the headline real space: drop it by about one row-gap, or cut the grid to 12 larger icons with bigger labels, so the type block and the joke can breathe and the labels read on the body.

designs.title: How to Go to Bed
designs.why: The best of the three. Loose brush drawings with real character, a warm serif title and italic captions, and a gag that builds through the repetition (four Turn around.) to the payoff 7. Sigh. It feels like an independent-label illustration tee, not clip art. It works on both black and white. Weak spots: steps 3 and 4 are anatomically confusing (head and body hard to parse), so the turning reads less clearly than it should. The captions get small on the body.
designs.fix: Redraw steps 3 and 4 so each one clearly shows the dog mid-spin (readable head, tail and direction, maybe a small motion arc) so the four turns read as one escalating sequence.

designs.title: The Box
designs.why: The story is universally relatable, and the panel-3 box breaking out of its frame is a good move. The happy cat in the box is the emotional hit. But line weights clash: panels 1 and 2 are fine, while panel 3 is heavy, and the dense tabby stripes in the small panels risk filling in on press. Panel 2's cat reads as curious rather than ignoring the bed. The frame lines tangle behind the flap and bed at the right. BOX NOT SOLD SEPARATELY. is a slightly fuzzy punchline set too small for the art above it.
designs.fix: Unify the line weight across all three panels and make panel 2 an unmistakable snub (cat turned away, tail up). Then tighten the caption to a crisper line set larger, e.g. bigger type under the panels.
